description:
The dependency batch failure envelope takes each edge's code from the shared classifier, and the gate checker renderer reads its lines from a table, so neither keeps a parallel copy of a decision made elsewhere.

## Background

`dependency_batch_json_error` in `crates/jit/src/output/failure.rs` builds the envelope for a rejected `jit dep add` batch. Its per-edge closure re-derives error codes that `classify_code` already assigns, so the batch path and the single-edge path can drift. `render_checker` in `crates/jit/src/output/gate.rs` doubles every arm on a `preset` flag. Handlers in `dispatch/claim.rs`, `recover` and `dispatch/doc.rs` repeat the same conversion of displayable warnings into outcome warnings.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each rejected edge in the `jit dep add` batch envelope carries the code the shared classifier assigns its error, plus the dependency-specific fallback for an error the classifier leaves generic. No second code-derivation closure remains.
- [hard] REQ-02: The batch envelope's shape, codes, exit status and suggestions are unchanged for every case the existing failure and CLI contract tests cover, and those tests pass unweakened.
- [hard] REQ-03: `render_checker` produces each line from one table of (kind, preset and plain text), with byte-identical output.
- [hard] REQ-04: Outcome warnings built from displayable values go through one shared conversion instead of a per-handler `map(ToString::to_string)`.
- [hard] REQ-05: The change removes at least 50 production lines from `crates/jit/src` (default mode of `scripts/production-lines.py`).

## Notes

Part of the epic's net-reduction work (plan D-51).
title: Dependency batch codes and checker text come from one source
